findings.summary: Premature abstraction is explained with a vague, partly circular cause and the 'Cost and cause' section mixes several ideas in dense one-line bullets.
findings.evidence:
Cause of each
God object = too many responsibilities. Spaghetti = tangled flow. Hammer = wrong tool. Premature = speculative structure.
findings.fix: Turn the four-in-one line into a Smell | Cause table, or four separate one-line bullets.

findings.summary: Page 1 diagram text 'Symptom / Cause / Refactor' is introduced without connecting it to the table, and the 'Signal' column for Premature abstraction ('guessed shape') is not a visible symptom.
findings.evidence: Premature abstraction | interface, factory or generic with one user | guessed shape
findings.fix: Make the Signal for premature abstraction observable, e.g. 'abstraction with one implementation; parameters nobody varies'.

findings.summary: YAGNI is used as a technique name but is never spelled out or explained.
findings.fix: Expand it on first use: "YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It): don't build for needs that don't exist yet".

findings.summary: The 'Cause vs Signal' table on page 2 lists causes under the Signal heading, so the same words mean different things than on page 1.
findings.evidence:
Anti-pattern | Signal | Fix
God object | too many responsibilities | split by SRP
findings.fix: Rename the column to 'Cause' or reuse the page 1 signals (thousands of lines, one tool everywhere) so Signal and Cause stay distinct.

findings.summary: Several bullets hold more than one idea.
findings.evidence:
Spaghetti: tests first, so the refactor is safe
Remove shared mutable state; Wrong abstraction: It costs more than duplication. Inline it back, then re-extract.
findings.fix: Split into one-idea bullets, e.g. 'Write tests first' and 'Remove shared mutable state'; separate the cost statement from the inline-and-re-extract fix.

findings.summary: Singleton code is shown under the heading before the one-line idea about its drawbacks; the injection snippet lacks a leading statement of the idea.
findings.fix: Add a one-line lead-in before each snippet, e.g. 'Pass the single instance in through the constructor'.

findings.summary: Code is shown before the one-line idea for the holder and enum variants, and the DCL block follows only a heading.
findings.fix: State the idea first (e.g. 'Holder: class loads on first getInstance(), so lazy and lock-free') before each snippet, and show holder and enum as separate blocks.

findings.summary: Bullets combine multiple ideas, and the Enum lazy claim is stated inconsistently across pages.
findings.evidence:
Enum: most robust (Effective Java); safe against reflection and serialization
Enum | on class use | none
Holder | first call | none (page 4) vs Holder | yes | none (page 6)
findings.fix: Split the robustness bullet into reflection and serialization points, and use the same Lazy wording for Holder in both tables ('first call').

findings.summary: Cheat sheet repeats the full DCL code and prose that duplicate the table, adding length without new content.
findings.evidence:
DCL locks only while instance is null; then one volatile read, no lock
Holder: no lock at all, class initialization is thread-safe
findings.fix: Drop the bullets that restate table cells, and keep only the snippet or a one-line pointer.
